identity.what_it_is: A 22 km stretch of white sand beach on the Indian Ocean, and the name of the suburb surrounding it, in the Shire of Broome, Western Australia, 4 km west of the Broome CBD.
identity.where: Broome, Western Australia, Australia (17.952226 S, 122.205577 E)
aliases: Walmanyjun (name used in official foreshore redevelopment branding)
identity.warnings: No slug/name mismatch in this bundle, but the name is shared with unrelated beaches in Cornwall (Porthcurno) and the Bahamas (Cable Beach, Bahamas) per Wikipedia's own disambiguation note; nearby but distinct beaches (Reddell Beach, Simpsons Beach, Gantheaume Point) are sometimes bundled into 'Cable Beach' content and should not be conflated with it.

spike_candidates.statement: Cable Beach nudists have shared their 'north of the rocks' strip with camel tours since the 1960s; regulars have dwindled to three or four.
spike_candidates.tension: A landmark naturist tradition is being quietly squeezed out by the same tourism boom that made the beach famous.

spike_candidates.statement: Cable Beach's only vehicle ramp closed in June 2025 and won't reopen until mid/late 2026 for a foreshore redevelopment.
spike_candidates.tension: The 'beloved Broome tradition' of driving onto the beach is suspended for over a year with no fixed reopening date.

spike_candidates.statement: Irukandji jellyfish shut Cable Beach in both 2010 and 2015, despite its marketing as a gentle, safe family beach.
spike_candidates.tension: The postcard 'gentle waves' beach is also a genuine venomous-jellyfish risk zone that tourism copy glosses over.

spike_candidates.statement: Cable Beach's marketed dinosaur-footprint age flips between 130 million years (Wikipedia) and 120 million years (visitor guide).
spike_candidates.tension: Even the site's headline fossil age can't be pinned down between the encyclopedia and the official tourism board.

facts.fact: Cable Beach is a 22 km stretch of white sand beach on the eastern Indian Ocean and the name of the surrounding suburb of Broome, 4 km west of the Broome CBD.
facts.quote: cable beach is a 22 km (14 mi) stretch of white sand beach on the eastern indian ocean and the name of the surrounding suburb in broome, western australia.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Cable Beach was named after the telegraph cable laid between Broome and Java in 1889.
facts.quote: cable beach was named after the telegraph cable laid between broome and java in 1889.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The Cable Beach suburb had a population of 5,436 at the 2016 census.
facts.quote: in 2016, the population was 5,436.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Gantheaume Point sits at the extreme southern end of Cable Beach and its lighthouse is a spot for observing dolphins and migrating whales.
facts.quote: gantheaume point is located at the extreme southern end of the beach.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Dinosaur footprints estimated at 130 million years old are visible in the rocks near Cable Beach at low tide, per Wikipedia.
facts.quote: dinosaur footprints estimated at 130 million years old are visible in the rocks at low tides.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Minyirr Park, adjacent to the southern section of Cable Beach, is a coastal reserve protecting the traditional land of the Yawuru people.
facts.quote: minyirr park is located adjacent to the southern section of the beach with walking trails that traverse the area behind the red ochre dunes.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Box jellyfish (stingers) may be present at Cable Beach between November and April, requiring caution when swimming.
facts.quote: box jellyfish, also known as stingers, may be present between november and april and caution is required when swimming there during this period.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: In January 1989, Broome News reported four beachgoers were stung by jellyfish at Cable Beach and required treatment at Broome District Hospital.
facts.quote: the january 1989 edition of broome news noted the recent stinging of four beachgoers by the jellyfish, who required treatment at broome district hospital.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Crocodiles have occasionally been sighted off Cable Beach's shore, prompting preventative measures.
facts.quote: there have been cases where crocodiles have been sighted off the shore occasionally and preventative measures are taken.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Cable Beach is home to one of Australia's most famous nudist (clothes-optional) beaches.
facts.quote: cable beach is home to one of australia's most famous nudist beaches.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The clothes-optional area is north of the beach access road from the car park and continues 17 km to the mouth of Willie Creek.
facts.quote: the clothes-optional area is to the north of the beach access road from the car park and continues to the mouth of willie creek, 17 km (11 mi) away.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Four-wheel drive vehicles are permitted north of the rocks at Cable Beach, allowing exploration of the beach at low tide.
facts.quote: four-wheel drive vehicles are permitted north of the rocks.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Camel rides on Cable Beach are available around sunrise and sunset hours.
facts.quote: camel rides are available around sunrise and sunset hours.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The Cable Beach suburb contains a government primary school, Cable Beach Primary School.
facts.quote: the suburb contains a government primary school, cable beach primary school.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Cable Beach falls in the state electorate of Kimberley and the federal division of Durack, postcode 6726.
facts.quote: state electorate kimberley • federal division durack postcode 6726
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: On 10 May 2010, potentially deadly Irukandji jellyfish forced the closure of Cable Beach after two stings over the weekend.
facts.quote: the broome shire has warned swimmers to be vigilant after potentially deadly irukandji jellyfish forced the closure of cable beach at the weekend.
facts.source_title: Irukandji stings close Cable Beach - The West Australian

facts.fact: A tourist was stung while swimming around noon on the Saturday, closing the beach through to Gantheaume Point; a local resident was also stung about 2pm while attending to their boat.
facts.quote: beach inspector tim trew said a tourist was stung while swimming about noon on saturday and the beach was closed through to gantheaume point.
facts.source_title: Irukandji stings close Cable Beach - The West Australian

facts.fact: Cable Beach reopened the Sunday morning after the May 2010 closure, once a net drag came up clear of jellyfish.
facts.quote: the beach was reopened on sunday morning, after a net drag came up clear.
facts.source_title: Irukandji stings close Cable Beach - The West Australian

facts.fact: Beach inspector Tim Trew said the May 2010 incident was the fourth Irukandji sting of the season on Cable Beach, against a seasonal average of about five.
facts.quote: that's the fourth sting we've had this season and we average about five,
facts.source_title: Irukandji stings close Cable Beach - The West Australian

facts.fact: On 10 September 2015, Shire of Broome lifeguards caught an Irukandji jellyfish during a routine stinger net drag, closing Cable Beach.
facts.quote: shire of broome lifeguards caught the jellyfish on thursday morning during a routine stinger net drag near the west australian beach.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach in Broome closed after Irukandji jellyfish scare - ABC News (via MSN)

facts.fact: Senior lifeguard Johnny Hardbattle described the September 2015 jellyfish as a fully grown Irukandji, about the size of a thumbnail with four tentacles from each corner.
facts.quote: it was a fully grown irukandji jellyfish, which is about the size of your thumbnail with four distinct tentacles coming off each corner,
facts.source_title: Cable Beach in Broome closed after Irukandji jellyfish scare - ABC News (via MSN)

facts.fact: As of the September 2015 closure, there had not been an Irukandji sting in Broome since the previous April.
facts.quote: there has not been an irukandji sting in broome since april.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach in Broome closed after Irukandji jellyfish scare - ABC News (via MSN)

facts.fact: Naturists have gathered on Cable Beach's 'north of the rocks' section since the 1960s to sunbake, fish and swim in the nude.
facts.quote: since the 1960s, naturists have gathered on a section of broome's famous cable beach known as "north of the rocks", to sunbake, fish and swim in the nude.
facts.source_title: Broome nudists battle to keep slice of beach as naturism's popularity declines - ABC News

facts.fact: By 2016, a local nudist said only three or four regulars still came down to the once-crowded 'north of the rocks' section.
facts.quote: so now there's only three or four of us that come down here regularly.
facts.source_title: Broome nudists battle to keep slice of beach as naturism's popularity declines - ABC News

facts.fact: As of 2016, Cable Beach's three camel tour companies operated within the same 100-metre stretch as the clothing-optional nudist section.
facts.quote: it's also the same 100 metres in which the beach's three camel tour companies operate, meaning there are hundreds more sets of peering eyes moving slowly past.
facts.source_title: Broome nudists battle to keep slice of beach as naturism's popularity declines - ABC News

facts.fact: Cable Beach is washed by tides that can reach over nine metres, described as providing a safe swimming environment.
facts.quote: washed clean every day by tides that can reach over nine metres, cable beach provides the ideal safe environment for swimming and relaxation.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Kimberley Australia

facts.fact: The Staircase to the Moon phenomenon, caused by a full moon rising over exposed Roebuck Bay mudflats, occurs for 3 nights every month per this source.
facts.quote: staircase to the moon is a natural phenomenon is caused by a full moon rising over the exposed mudflats of roebuck bay at extremely low tides, creating a beautiful optical illusion of a staircase reaching to the moon.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Kimberley Australia

facts.fact: Per this source, camel rides have a 120kg per-person weight limit and the camel train can accommodate up to 36 riders at once.
facts.quote: the camel train can accommodate up to 36 riders at one time.
facts.source_title: Cable Beach - Kimberley Australia

facts.fact: Broome has two camel tour operators on Cable Beach, distinguished by blanket colour: Red Sun Camels (red) and Broome Camel Safaris (blue).
facts.quote: broome has two camel tour operators, each with a different colour blankets. red sun camels is famously red. broome camel safaris have the blue blankets.
facts.source_title: Camel Rides - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: As of 2026, all Cable Beach camel ride operators enforce a 90kg individual weight limit.
facts.quote: please be advised that there is a 90kg individual weight limit that is being enforced by all camel ride operators.
facts.source_title: Camel Rides - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: The Broome Visitor Centre also states Cable Beach is 22km of pristine white sand and clear tropical waters.
facts.quote: cable beach is 22kms of pristine white sand and clear tropical waters.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: Broome's dinosaur footprints (marketed alongside Cable Beach) are described as 120 million years old, tracking about 80km along the coast from south of Broome up the Dampier Peninsula.
facts.quote: the dinosaur footprints around broome (rubibi) are recognised as the most significant in the world with track ways stretching for about 80km along broome's sandstone coast line from south of broome up along the dampier peninsula.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: Per the Broome Visitor Centre, Staircase to the Moon happens 2-3 days a month between March and October (contrast with F27's '3 nights').
facts.quote: the staircase to the moon happens 2 - 3 days a month between march and october.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: The Cable Beach vehicle access ramp has been closed since 3 June 2025 until mid/late 2026 for the Walmanyjun Cable Beach foreshore redevelopment Stage 2.
facts.quote: cable beach ramp closure - effective from 3 june 2025 until mid/late 2026.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: Stage 1 of the Walmanyjun Cable Beach foreshore redevelopment is complete; Stage 2 is underway, adding a community plaza and improved event spaces.
facts.quote: stage 1 is now complete. stage 2 is underway - bringing a new community plaza, improved event spaces, and enhanced accessibility to the famous cable beach shoreline.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: During the Stage 2 works, there is no vehicle access to north of the rocks; pedestrian access to that section and the camels is via the surf club beach access point only.
facts.quote: there will be no vehicle access point onto cable beach to north of the rocks, with pedestrian access only to north of the rocks and camels via the surf club beach access point.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: The speed limit for vehicles driving on Cable Beach near Gantheaume Point and north of the rocks is 15km/h.
facts.quote: the speed limit for vehicles driving on both cable beach both near gantheaume point and north of the rocks is 15km/h.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: A gate has been installed at the Cable Beach amphitheatre that is locked when vehicle access is not permitted and during turtle nesting season.
facts.quote: a gate has been installed at the cable beach amphitheatre and will be locked when vehicle access is not permitted and also during turtle nesting season.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: The Shire of Broome, with West Coast Water Safety and the Broome Surf Life Saving Club, does not patrol Cable Beach during the tropical season (usually late October to early April).
facts.quote: during the tropical season months (usually late october until early april), broome's beaches are not patrolled by lifeguards.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: During the dry season, there are daily lifeguard patrols of the Cable Beach swimming area marked by red and yellow flags.
facts.quote: during the dry season there are daily patrols of the swimming area on cable beach marked by red and yellow flags in front of the broome surf life saving club.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: Lifeguards are scheduled to return to Cable Beach on Good Friday, 3 April 2026.
facts.quote: lifeguards return to cable beach on good friday, 3rd april 2026.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: The lighthouse at Gantheaume Point, near Cable Beach, was built in 1905, one of ten lighthouses built on the WA coast between 1900 and 1913.
facts.quote: the lighthouse at gantheaume point was built in 1905 and was " one of ten lighthouses built on the west australian coast between 1900 and 1913" according to the heritage council of western australia.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: Anastasia's Pool, a rockpool carved out by a lighthouse keeper at Gantheaume Point for his arthritic wife, was damaged by a storm in 2014.
facts.quote: anastasia's pool was damaged by a storm in 2014.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: The walk from Cable Beach to Gantheaume Point is about 5km.
facts.quote: the walk from cable beach to gantheaume point is about 5km.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

facts.fact: Cable Beach is the iconic location of major tourism events including the Shinju Matsuri long table dinner.
facts.quote: cable beach is also the iconic location of several major tourism events, including the shinju matsuri long table dinner.
facts.source_title: Highlights of Broome - Broome Visitor Centre

conflicts: Dinosaur footprint age: Wikipedia says footprints near Cable Beach are 'estimated at 130 million years old' (F05) vs the Broome Visitor Centre's 'discover 120 million year old dinosaur footprints!' (F32).

Camel ride weight limit: kimberley-australia.com states a 120kg per-person weight limit and a 36-rider capacity (F28) vs the current (2026) Broome Visitor Centre page enforcing a 90kg individual weight limit (F30) - likely a policy change over time, but the older figure is undated so it can't be confirmed as superseded rather than simply wrong.
Staircase to the Moon frequency: kimberley-australia.com says the phenomenon occurs 'for 3 nights every month' (F27) vs the Broome Visitor Centre's 'happens 2 - 3 days a month' (F33).
